title: 3D Neural Tissue Printing Protocol Using BIO X and Pneumatic Printhead
author: Chrenek, Kirsch, et al.
materials: Lack of or inconsistent material extrusion, problem

steps.title: Prepare crosslinked bioink
steps.instruction: Mix 1 mL of TissuePrint‑HV bioink with 3–5 mL of TissuePrint Crosslinker (≈3–5 mL crosslinker per 1 mL bioink) to obtain up to three 10 × 10 mm cylindrical prints at 25 % infill; target cell density is 1 × 10⁶ cells / mL (≈200 000–350 000 cells per construct) but 0.5–5 × 10⁶ cells / mL are acceptable.

steps.title: Make non‑sterile agarose solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 0.5 % agarose solution in distilled water using a stir plate set to 70 °C and 350–400 rpm; cover the bottle, mix for 3–4 h until clear, then turn off heat and increase stirring to 900 rpm as the mixture cools to ~20‑22 °C, keep on the hot plate for another 3–4 h until it begins to thicken, yielding a smooth translucent liquid (viscosity between water and syrup). Store at 4 °C for up to one week.

substeps.instruction: Place distilled water in a bottle on a stir plate heated to 70 °C; add agarose while stirring at 350–400 rpm (agarose must not be microwaved).
Cover the bottle to prevent debris and evaporation.
Stir for 3–4 h until agarose is fully dissolved and the solution is no longer cloudy.
Turn off heat; increase stirring speed to 900 rpm as temperature drops to ~20‑22 °C.
Continue stirring on the hot plate for 3–4 h until the mixture begins to thicken and attains a smooth, translucent consistency.
Store the non‑sterile agarose at 4 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: Make sterile agarose solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a sterile 0.5 % agarose solution by autoclaving the agarose‑water mixture (121 °C, 30 min), then while still >80 °C place it on a hot plate at 900 rpm and stir for 3–4 h until it begins to thicken; store at 4 °C for up to one week.

substeps.instruction: Place distilled water in an autoclavable bottle, add agarose, and insert a stir rod.
Autoclave at 121 °C for 30 min.
When temperature is still above 80 °C, remove the bottle and immediately place it on a hot plate set to 900 rpm.
Stir for 3–4 h until the solution begins to thicken.
Store the sterile agarose at 4 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: Set up printer and decontaminate
steps.instruction: Autoclave all lab equipment, place the BIO X printer inside a sterile biosafety cabinet (BSC) and plug it in, decontaminate the printer and BSC with MycoClean Mycoplasma Prevention Spray, Conflikt™ and 70 % ethanol, power on the printer, run the BIO X UV chamber cleaning routine via the Utilities menu, then UV‑irradiate the entire BSC (door closed, wear UV safety glasses). Recommended equipment: for agarose support bath – two conical racks, two spatulas, wash bottle, 1 mL pipette, two waste beakers; for direct‑plate printing – two conical racks, two spatulas, 1 mL pipette, two waste beakers.

substeps.instruction: Autoclave any lab equipment that will be used.
Place the BIO X printer in a sterile BSC and connect the power cord.
Decontaminate the BIO X and the BSC using MycoClean Mycoplasma Prevention Spray, Conflikt™, and 70 % ethanol.
Turn on the BIO X using the power switch on the back panel (right‑hand side when viewed from the front).
Perform UV sterilization of the BIO X chamber: open the Utilities (gear) menu, select “Clean chamber”, turn on the “Clean chamber fan”, and click “Start”.
UV‑irradiate the entire BSC with its built‑in UV source or an external one; keep the BIO X door closed and wear UV protective safety glasses.

steps.title: Print onto cell culture plate
steps.instruction: Using the BIO X, print the bioink directly onto a cell‑culture plate (or Petri dish) with the printhead tip ~0.1 mm above the surface; set calibration height 0.1 mm, print speed 15 mm/s, pressure 11 kPa (Table 2). If the construct does not hold shape, optionally coat the well with crosslinker before printing. After printing, pipette enough crosslinker onto the well edges to fully submerge the construct (do not apply directly onto the construct), let it sit 2–3 min (or until gelled), remove excess crosslinker, then transfer the construct to a new (pre‑coated if needed) plate and add cell‑culture media (or tris‑buffered saline for cell‑free constructs). Optional: media or TBS can be added to the original plate instead of transferring.

substeps.instruction: Press “Print” on the BIO X touchscreen.
Position the printhead tip ~0.1 mm above the cell‑culture plate or Petri dish.
Adjust speed and pressure as needed (target: 15 mm/s speed, 11 kPa pressure) to achieve a steady, even extrusion.
Optional: coat the well with crosslinker before printing if the construct does not retain shape.
When the print finishes, pipette crosslinker onto the edges of the well—enough to submerge the construct, avoiding direct application onto the printed structure.
Allow the construct to remain in the crosslinker for 2–3 min (or until the material gels and holds its shape).
Remove the crosslinker from the well using a pipette.
Transfer the construct to a new (pre‑coated if applicable) cell‑culture plate and fill the well with appropriate cell‑culture media; for cell‑free prints, use tris‑buffered saline (TBS).
Optional: add TBS or media directly to the original plate instead of transferring, if a pre‑coated plate is not required.
